thread.title: BlackRock: Cheaper, Growing Faster And It Generates Better Returns Than The Overall Market - BlackRock, Inc. (NYSE:BLK) | Seeking Alpha

author: Dale Roberts
title: BlackRock: Cheaper, Growing Faster And It Generates Better Returns Than The Overall Market - BlackRock, Inc. (NYSE:BLK) | Seeking Alpha
text:
For US holdings I skimmed 15 of the largest cap Dividend Achievers ( VIG ), you can read about that adventure in this article Buying Dividend Growth Stocks Without Looking .
As I stated in that article, I may have considered skimming 20 of the largest cap Achievers but given that I have 3 US picks by way of Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), BlackRock ( BLK ) and Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.B ), I consider the total US group of 18 is 'enough'. My picks are based on very simple themes or investment trends. For BlackRock, that undeniable trend is the massive move from higher fee actively managed funds to lower fee ETF Model Portfolios . Many 'stock pickers' are certainly adding ETF assets to their portfolios for quick and easy diversification. We see many self-directed stock pickers make the full move to these simple ETF Portfolios. One can create a complete globally diversified portfolio with a management expense ration in the range of .10%-15%.
BLK is more than well positioned for that massive move and is in fact the global leader with iShares. ETF assets are set to potentially double over the next 5 years and BLK might be there to grab a significant percentage of those assets. While the MERs (Management Expense Ratios) are very low, there are great revenues and profits to be had simply based on scale. We are talking hundreds of billions to trillions of dollars of assets over the next 5 years, 10 years and beyond.
It's an undeniable and IMHO unstoppable trend that is only likely to continue. Passive indexing and smart beta index funds simply offer a superior way to invest. I like to cheekily remark that With This Stock I Beat The Market Because Most Investors Can't Beat The Market. Oh, The Irony.
Yes an investor who has been in the stock for the last several years would have a nice market ( IVV ) beat. This is a period where we have seen the greatest flows to passive investments. Portfolio 1 is BlackRock. The chart is courtesy of portfoliovisualizer.com The period is January of 2012 to end of November 2018.
The investors who have been in BlackRock over the last 2-3 years would have seen that market beat disappear. The stock has been hit hard as fears of market corrections and market volatility has returned.
That said, the long historical financials look rock solid. The headline was borrowed from a few lines of copy in this Seeking Alpha article BlackRock: Crown Jewel + Hidden Gem = Opportunity from Manole Capital Management. That article offers a wonderful overview of the business lines - the where and how BlackRock makes monies. From below, we see that BlackRock generates 51% of fund revenues from Index products and 49% from the active funds.
BlackRock also operates in the institutional active space with its proprietary Aladdin analytical platform.
From that article …
While Aladdin represents just 5% of BlackRock’s revenues, this platform would garner a much higher valuation on its own, if it was a stand-alone business. The Aladdin business used to be primarily focused on the fixed income market, but it has been diversifying towards equities and other multi-asset classes. Since 2012, BlackRock has doubled the number of countries where Aladdin is in used and outside the US now represents 30% of its revenue.
From the article comment section, a reader adds …
Aladdin is basically a monopoly on end-to-end fixed income portfolio management software. Bloomberg/POINT may someday compete but Aladdin is far more mature as an OMS/Compliance/Operations management system and I doubt anyone will be able to catch up.
I just love hearing that Monopoly word.
This Financial Times articles states Aladdin is The genie in BlackRock's Money Machine and offers …
Questions about Aladdin’s potential influence on global markets make sense in light of its scale and complexity. Aladdin holds detailed information relating to every asset or security “in the investable universe”, the company said. BlackRock employs 1,000 staff worldwide to keep this information accurate and up to date. What makes it so powerful is how it uses that information to aid portfolio managers.
Aladdin is making generous contributions to revenue and earnings. From the Manole Capital article, after stating that BlackRock had beat the market in 5 of the 6 years from 2012 to 2017 …
2017 was a great year for BlackRock. The stock was up 38%, well in excess of the overall market. Revenues grew an impressive double-digits (+12% year-over-year) and earnings were up in the high-teens (+17% year-over-year). It generated significant free cash flow, which management used to lift its dividend by 15% to a respectable +2.5% yield. In addition, BlackRock re-purchased $900 million of its own stock.
With the recent market correction and more exaggerated share price decline for BlackRock, the current yield available is now 3.4% according to Seeking Alpha's dividend page. At current prices, one receives a very generous (market beating) dividend and very generous dividend growth. From the BlackRock Investor page.
Guru Focus states that the average 5-year dividend growth rate is 10.9%.
Is BlackRock one of the next Dividend Achievers? The company has now increased its dividend for 8 years running. If it can pass the dividend health screens we might see the company join the index. It would likely be there today, but it did hold its dividend in the financial crisis. That's a considerable gold star performance for a financial company through a financial crisis. It was in the crises that BlackRock acquired the iShares franchise from Barclays in more than opportunistic fashion. That move was Buffettesque.
And also form Guru Focus when you purchase BlackRock at current prices you are picking up a 9.45% earnings yield. The forward rate of return based on cash flow history (The Yachtman score) is 11%.
And here are the key stats from Morningstar.
I am a pretty simple guy when it comes to investing. Again I only have 3 picks for the US market and I look for a simple theme and then the additional 'research' that I might do is look at the basic revenue and earnings history and apply that against the broader overarching theme. BlackRock is poised to continue to take advantage of the investing revolution known as indexing.
We see increasing revenues, increasing profits, increasing dividends, increasing book value and increasing cash flows. Check, check, check and more checks. The payout ratio for the dividends looks quite consistent and it remains in a very comfortable band.
This paints the picture perhaps of not a massive growth story, but a very rock solid growth story.
Manole Capital frames the overall investment story and future prospects as ...
We believe BlackRock’s business model is much more sustainable than the average US company. It does not have any issues with fluctuating commodity costs or inflationary pressures. It is experiencing positive regulatory change and is one of the few companies actually benefitting from new Washington DC rules. It is a clear market leader and has durable competitive advantages. There are high barriers to entry and a wide moat around its franchise.
Once again I love hearing that moat word and concept.
According to my TD Waterhouse overviews and analyst consensus, the company is more than well regarded, and is recommended.
A Morningstar report suggests that the company is "Undervalued"
Once again, I will stick to those simple charts detailing the revenue and profit history, but if you want to read up on the market makers and their educated guess on the future prospects for BlackRock, knock yourself out. I think you'll find that the overall collective guess leads to a very positive outlook.
While the analysts don't know the future, and we don't know the future I feel very confident with my BlackRock investment. I feel there is a very strong probability that the company will continue to deliver over the longer term.
That said, the price risks and volatility for BLK might continue to be greater than the broader market due to the potential of negative outflows and lower fees generated during market corrections. Shareholders might be in for a rough ride in the short term; but if they can embrace the volatility and accumulate (value hunting), they might be rewarded with more market beating returns over the longer term and through market cycles.
Author's note: Thanks for reading. Please always know and invest within your risk tolerance level. Always know all tax implications and consequences. If you liked this article, please hit that "Like" button.
Disclosure: I am/we are long BNS, TD, RY, AAPL, NKE, BCE, TU, ENB, TRP, CVS, WBA, MSFT, MMM, CL, JNJ, QCOM, MDT, BRK.B, ABT, PEP, TXN, WMT, BLK.
